<div class="eyebrow">Comparative product review · September 4, 2026 · Recommendations only</div>

# Make the next set the obvious thing.

<p class="lede">My Workout Pal and Trainpal share a capable workout engine. Both make the person training manage too much interface. The strongest next step is a full UI redesign around starting, logging, resting, and returning.</p>

<nav class="report-nav" aria-label="Report sections"><a href="#verdict">Verdict</a><a href="#journeys">Observed journeys</a><a href="#videos">Video evidence</a><a href="#redesign">Full redesign</a><a href="#prototype">Try the concept</a><a href="#roadmap">Recommendations</a><a href="#evidence">Evidence and limits</a></nav>

<div class="verdict" id="verdict"><div class="eyebrow">Recommendation</div><p class="lede">Keep the useful domain and recovery behavior. Replace the screen hierarchy, navigation, workout interaction, visual language, and asset system from scratch.</p><p>Trainpal improves the public invitation and some labels, but adds friction before training and has a reproduced local onboarding defect. MWP has a less obstructed member home and more truthful interrupted-history semantics. Neither earns an overall flow victory.</p></div>

<div class="metrics"><div class="metric"><strong>≈2,500 px</strong><span>Both mobile runners place the first weight field almost three viewport heights into the document.</span></div><div class="metric"><strong>+665 px</strong><span>Trainpal places day choices farther down its first-use member home than MWP in the matched fixture.</span></div><div class="metric"><strong>134 / 134</strong><span>Both live catalogs render a primary demonstration and two title tabs for every movement.</span></div></div>

These measurements describe the audited states at 390 × 844 CSS pixels, not physical-device timings. The signed-in pages ran in isolated production-built synthetic fixtures. Public pages were checked on both live origins. Scores and design preferences are expert judgments, not user-study results.

**Primary persona:** a recreational lifter using a phone between sets, with ordinary app familiarity and limited attention. The first-time visitor lens also covers understanding the example and creating a routine.

## Comparative scorecard

Flow has the greatest influence on the assessment. The scale is 1–10: 1 means blocked, 3 means substantial coaching is needed, 5 means completable with friction, 7 means mostly self-evident, and 9 means consistently low effort. Half-points express judgment, not measurement precision. No weighted overall score is used because the onboarding defect and shared runner friction matter more than a small aesthetic difference.

| Dimension | MWP | Trainpal | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intuitive flow — highest priority | 4.5 | 4.5 | Both expose planning and system mechanics before the next training action. Trainpal improves entry but worsens the first-use member hierarchy. |
| Ease of use | 5 | 4.5 | Both reached saved/completed states; Trainpal setup bypassed equipment confirmation. Trainpal’s step-two Continue unexpectedly submitted onboarding in two fresh local scopes. |
| Gym usefulness | 4.5 | 4.5 | Saved sets, drafts, timers, and resume survive reload. Logging, rest, set selection, and movement completion remain separate tasks. Live catalog coverage is equal. |
| Visual hierarchy | 5.5 | 6 | Trainpal’s public scene is more cohesive, but both have dense text, repeated boxes, and oversized demonstration controls. |
| Images and character integration | 5 | 6 | MWP’s mascot occupies an isolated strip. Trainpal’s scene better establishes a place, but neither connects art consistently to the training flow. |

### What each app does better

**Reuse from Trainpal:** the direct public invitation to create a plan, clearer routine terminology, quieter utility links, explicit video expansion inventory, origin-aware player helper, and a cohesive environmental illustration direction. Its underlying video IDs are useful evidence to reconcile with live data.

**Preserve from MWP:** the shorter route to member day choices, the recent distinction between unfinished and deliberately skipped exercises, and the deletion of unused progression code. Preserve the shared immutable workout snapshots, server ownership checks, unit storage, saved-set recovery, selected-set recovery, and running timer recovery.

**Replace in both:** the public sample dead end, management-first home, revision-oriented editing language, oversized reference material in the runner, fragmented set/rest progression, and progress summaries that communicate little after a bodyweight workout.

<div class="pair"><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="mwp home phone" width="375" height="812" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>MWP · live public home.</strong> The heading and small isolated companion strip do not explain the actual training interaction.</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="trainpal home phone" width="375" height="812" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>Trainpal · live public home.</strong> A more coherent setting and direct creation invitation. This advantage does not carry through the signed-in hierarchy.</figcaption></figure></div>

### The five changes with the greatest immediate value

1. **H1 · Prevent accidental onboarding submission.** A Continue action must not create a routine with default equipment.
2. **H2 · Bring the set logger into the first viewport.** Remove the overview and video stack from the path to every work set.
3. **M1 · Put Start or Resume first on Today.** Delete the permanent teaching blocks before changing their styling.
4. **M2 · Make “Try sample workout” a usable trial or rename it.** A completed snapshot cannot demonstrate the promised interaction.
5. **M3 · Show actual completed sets and reps.** Give bodyweight sessions useful feedback without inventing load or time.

Unsupported progression copy and video provenance are separate content-truth corrections described in the report; aesthetic preferences remain design recommendations rather than extra defect counts.


<h2 id="journeys">What the journeys revealed</h2>

### Entry and the first useful moment

Both public sites let a visitor explore an example program, choose Push day, open a guide, return to the day, and select **Try sample workout**. That label opens a completed, read-only snapshot. The visitor cannot log a practice set or experience the rest loop. Three navigation activations from the example path still lead to passive explanation.

MWP prioritizes **Explore five-day example** and explains optional sign-in separately. Trainpal prioritizes **Create my workout plan** and sends the visitor to `/app`. Signed-out `/app` redirected to `/sign-in?returnTo=%2Fapp` in both live apps. Both sign-in screens expose Google, email, Register, and Recovery. No account submission or provider sign-in was performed.

**Recommendation:** offer a short **Try one set** experience using clearly disposable data. Use **Save my routine** when an account provides an immediate benefit. Retain the example as a secondary reference. Remove the unsupported sample-page claim that the active runner suggests load progression: MWP deleted the unused evaluator; Trainpal retains it without a caller. Neither inspected runner implements the advertised behavior.

### Setup and routine creation

MWP’s setup presents starting point, equipment, six substitution explanations, display units, a raw IANA time-zone field, and reduced motion in one long form. Trainpal attempts a three-step setup and detects the time zone, which is a reasonable reduction in effort.

However, Trainpal’s **Continue** on step two saved the routine before equipment selection. This occurred with both the example and blank starting points in fresh local scopes. The user chose metric units, clicked Continue once, and arrived at the saved home or editor without seeing step three or clicking the final creation action.

The likely cause is a same-position unkeyed button changing from `type="button"` to `type="submit"` during the click. The browser result is reproduced; this source mechanism is a strong hypothesis, not an instrumented causal proof or a production reproduction. The fix needs a focused test: step-two Continue reveals equipment and makes zero onboarding POSTs; only the final explicit action submits once.

<div class="pair"><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="trainpal blank step2" width="375" height="812" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>Before · local Trainpal.</strong> Units step, before one Continue activation.</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="trainpal blank after continue" width="375" height="812" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>After · same fresh scope.</strong> A saved blank routine appears in the editor. Equipment and final confirmation were bypassed.</figcaption></figure></div>

Both **blank** routes create Day 1, Main work, and Dead bug with three sets. The UI explains the placeholder, but the user cannot remove the only movement. A database publication invariant is defining the creation experience.

**Recommendation:** an empty editor should be truly empty. Keep an unpublished draft until the user adds a movement. Use **Add your first movement**, then **Save routine**. Hide section taxonomy until a user needs it. Preserve immutable revisions behind the interface when a routine is saved; do not make users manufacture valid training content to satisfy storage rules.

### Returning to train

The normal route is two activations: choose a saved day, then **Start or resume workout**. Before the day choice, MWP shows management and progress. Trainpal adds a personal-guidance callout and **How to use this home** checklist. That checklist stays until a completed workout, so an interrupted first workout still leaves teaching material before Resume.

At the same 390-pixel width, with the same example routine and no active workout, the day section began at approximately 1,000 CSS pixels in MWP and 1,665 in Trainpal. A small synthetic-fixture banner is present in both. This is a hierarchy problem, not merely a spacing problem.

<div class="pair"><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="mwp home full" width="375" height="2251" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>MWP · local member home.</strong> Scroll the evidence image to inspect the full hierarchy. Management and progress precede days.</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="trainpal home full" width="375" height="2915" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>Trainpal · matched local home.</strong> Additional explanation pushes days and resume farther down the page.</figcaption></figure></div>

**Recommendation:** show Resume first whenever a workout exists. Otherwise show the next chosen day, its equipment, and **Start workout**. Put the full routine, guidance, history, and settings behind stable navigation. Explain unfamiliar controls at the moment they are used; remove the permanent home tutorial.

### Logging, rest, and forward movement

The shared mobile runner begins with identifiers and snapshot explanations, a six-movement outline, and large demonstration tabs/player. The first weight input was at approximately 2,477 CSS pixels in MWP and 2,499 in Trainpal. Neither makes the main repeated task available on the initial phone screen.

Actual sequence in both: enter 10 kg and 10 reps → Save set → saved status, but no rest starts and selection stays put → manually start 1:30 rest → manually select set two → enter 11 kg and nine reps → reload. Both preserved the saved first set, unsubmitted second-set values, second-set selection, and running timer. That resilience is valuable.

After all three work sets were saved, **Complete exercise** marked completion but left the same exercise selected. Moving forward required choosing the next movement from the outline. An early completion attempt in MWP correctly rejected an incomplete exercise. Keep that domain protection while changing the interaction.

<div class="pair"><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="mwp runner full" width="388" height="4406" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>MWP · local runner.</strong> Identifiers, overview, and video controls occupy the document before logging.</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="trainpal runner full" width="388" height="4428" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>Trainpal · local runner.</strong> The same repeated training task has nearly the same scroll cost.</figcaption></figure></div>

**Recommendation:** place exercise name, target, recent performance when available, set rows, inputs appropriate to the target, and **Log set & rest** in the first viewport. Open cues and video in a secondary sheet. Keep the saved set visible during rest and make **Next set** explicit. After the final work set, offer **Next exercise**. Provide undo/edit and rest controls without making them compete with the primary action. Distinguish a local pending save from a confirmed server save.

### Editing, interruption, and completion

The movement chooser worked in both apps: replace Dead bug, search `push-up`, choose the canonical Push-up, then publish a one-set routine. Search context and guide return were preserved in the public library too. Both found five push-up variations while the equipment profile remained Dumbbells; **Compatible with Dumbbells** can be misread as a movement requiring dumbbells. Label the profile separately from actual required equipment.

After successful publication, the editor still displayed **Unpublished draft · base revision 2**, alongside **Draft matches active revision** and a published status. Replace these contradictory signals with **Saved**, **Unsaved changes**, **Saving**, or a specific failure. Show a revision comparison only when it helps confirm a consequential change.

Exit and Resume worked in both tested local runners. Abandoning led to History. MWP called remaining movements **unfinished**; Trainpal’s abandoned-workout handling labels pending work **skipped**. Deliberate skip and unattempted work should remain distinct facts. A completed one-set, 10-rep push-up workout reached History and Progress in both apps.

Both Progress screens then showed one completed workout but 0 kg·reps, 0 seconds, and 0 km. The totals are consistent with logged external load and timed/distance work, but they do not explain the value of 10 bodyweight reps. Do not fabricate load or duration. Show completed sets and reps, distinguish elapsed session time from prescribed timed exercise, and hide irrelevant zero cards.

<div class="pair"><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="mwp completed progress" width="375" height="812" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>MWP · completed synthetic push-up session.</strong> One completed workout is visible; the summary metrics mostly read zero.</figcaption></figure><figure><div class="shot"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="trainpal completed progress" width="375" height="812" loading="lazy"></div><figcaption><strong>Trainpal · same completed task.</strong> The shared metrics underserve bodyweight training.</figcaption></figure></div>

<h2 id="videos">Videos: reuse the evidence, correct the claims</h2>

The catalogs themselves are identical: 134 canonical movements. Trainpal adds 214 video mappings for 107 movements in source, preserving the 54 inherited rows. All 268 distinct video IDs returned live public YouTube oEmbed metadata during this audit. One concentration-curl title changed punctuation; channel attribution matched after trimming four trailing spaces.

The decisive distinction is between seed files and live pages:

| Evidence surface | My Workout Pal | Trainpal | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Checked-in seed | 54 videos / 27 movements | 268 videos / 134 movements | Reproducibility and source inventory |
| Public page sweep | 134/134 HTTP 200; primary iframe and both title tabs match | Same, with no exceptions | Equal rendered hosted coverage |
| All-ID oEmbed check | The shared 268-ID inventory returned metadata | Same inventory | Availability of metadata, not playback |
| Selected browser playback | Hosted expanded pair inspected on Push-up | Push-up video visually advanced; clean Demo 2 visually advanced | Selected playback and a concrete variation discrepancy |
| Full audiovisual watching | Not established | Not established | Neither approval flag proves a human viewing event |

The public sweep extracted actual rendered iframe elements and title-tab text, excluding serialized script data. It observed primary IDs; secondary IDs in the JSON inventory are expected IDs unless selected in the browser. It did not play all 268 embeds. MWP’s local fixture uses its narrower seed, so its text-only local push-up guide is not representative of hosted MWP coverage.

Trainpal’s documents describe shared Firebase/Neon infrastructure. The live results are consistent with shared data, and both repositories read approved videos from the database. Private database identity and causal deployment history were not verified. Do not blindly reseed the additions: both live apps already display them.

### What to reuse and what to change

Reuse Trainpal’s explicit slug-to-video mapping inventory and origin-aware embed helper. Preserve the inherited accessible video tabs, named iframe, no autoplay, privacy-enhanced embed host, and external YouTube fallback. Scope playback evidence to the actual origin and browser: successful metadata, a thumbnail, or an iframe alone does not establish playback. The [YouTube IFrame API reference](https://developers.google.com/youtube/iframe_api_reference) documents playback states and error handling.

Do not copy the expansion converter’s unconditional `fullWatchConfirmed: true`, `reviewer: product-owner`, fixed review date, or catalog-count-based approval promise. Its source research describes sampled contact sheets and no audio review. The inherited MWP rows also name AI reviewers, so apply the same skepticism to their human-watch claims. The problem is overstated provenance; it does not imply every selected demonstration is unsuitable.

**Recommended future policy change:** permit one useful, working demonstration with an optional alternate. Separate metadata checks, scoped playback, equipment/variation evidence, sampled visual review, full viewing, and editorial approval. A title-only match should remain a suggested external reference; a visually supported match with playback evidence can carry a modest **Demo** label. Focus additional review on ambiguous variations, complex movements, and user reports. The existing human-watch/pair policy remains in force until separately changed; no videos were approved, seeded, or published in this audit.

This removes repeated process without inventing stronger evidence. If one video fails, keep instructions and the surviving useful demo. Show **Watch demo**, **Another demo**, **Open on YouTube**, and **Report a problem**. Delete curation-process essays from the workout UI.

| Mapping | Evidence | Decision to resolve |

| Dumbbell snatch · `3mlhF3dptAo` / `R0mhHuVrLHA` | Research distinguishes power catch and overhead-squat catch. | Label meaningful variants instead of presenting an exact interchangeable pair. |
| Russian twist · `LlccOWys8IU` | Source describes a plate while catalog equipment is bodyweight. | Label optional load or lead with bodyweight. |
| Rack pull · `LSS670gHFfA` | Live title describes very high rack pulls with 737 pounds. | Review its value as instruction; do not infer beginner suitability from availability. |

<h2 id="redesign">A full UI redesign from scratch</h2>

<p class="lede">“Quiet Set” is a provisional visual direction, not a required product rename. It replaces the page system and art direction while preserving useful training data and recovery behavior.</p>

The design should feel like a calm training companion: a clear next action, a small amount of relevant guidance, and warmth around the edges. Every major screen gets a new hierarchy. New assets, backgrounds, characters, typography, spacing, icons, surfaces, and motion form one system. This is a comprehensive recommendation with concept artwork and a working simulation, not a production-ready redesign implementation.

<figure class="art"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="quiet set art direction" width="1536" height="1024" loading="lazy"><figcaption><strong>Original generated art direction.</strong> Pip, a stoat companion, in ready and complete poses; a dawn studio; and a restrained surface palette. Concept board, not exported production sprites.</figcaption></figure>

### Rebuild the information architecture

Use three persistent destinations: **Today**, **Routine**, and **Progress**. Put account, units, equipment profile, privacy, guidance management, and appearance in Settings. Make Library contextual: browse from Routine, add/replace from the editor, and open a guide from an exercise. Preserve the originating routine, search, selected exercise, and return destination.

<div class="flow" aria-label="Proposed main flow"><span>Today</span><span>Start or resume</span><span>Log set</span><span>Rest</span><span>Next set / exercise</span><span>Finish</span><span>Progress</span></div>

| Screen | New hierarchy and primary action | Important states and recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome | One promise, **Try one set**, secondary example and account access. Scene occupies a bounded supporting area. | Guest simulation clearly labeled; sign-in cancellation returns to context. |
| Setup | Choose example or empty routine; ask only what the chosen task needs. Infer time zone, make units editable. **Create routine** is a separate final action. | Back retains choices; equipment is confirmed when it changes actual movement selection. Error preserves inputs. |
| Today | Active workout Resume takes priority. Otherwise next selected day, equipment, and **Start workout**. | No routine: Add first movement. No completed workout: no zero-stat dashboard. Interrupted session retains last set. |
| Routine | Editable day list, movement rows, concise targets, **Add movement**. | Truly empty draft; Saved/Unsaved/Saving/Failed status. Deletion is undoable before save. Changes affecting an active workout explain that its snapshot stays unchanged. |
| Movement chooser | Search, equipment requirements, movement name, target type, concise cue. **Use movement**. | No results, unavailable media, custom movement, and cancel return to the same editor position. |
| Exercise guide | Name, specific variant, three concise cues, **Watch demo**, optional alternate. | Player failure offers external fallback; instructions remain usable. Avoid certification language. |
| Active workout | Exercise, target, optional last comparable performance, set rows, target-appropriate inputs, **Log set & rest**. | Pending/saved/error distinct. Validation next to field. Undo edits the intended set. No unsolicited load suggestion. |
| Rest | Timer, just-saved set, next target, **Next set**. | Pause, add time, skip rest, edit saved set. Countdown uses a deadline and survives suspension/reload. |
| Exercise transition | Completed sets and next movement, **Next exercise**. | Explicit skip reason optional; unattempted work remains unfinished. Routine order can still be changed deliberately. |
| Finish | Actual completed work and unfinished work, **Finish workout**. | Prevent duplicate completion; persist before confirmed success. Interrupted exit is separate from completion. |
| History and Progress | Recent sessions, sets/reps, meaningful movement trends; session detail is inspectable. | Bodyweight work receives useful credit without invented tonnage. Empty, interrupted, partial, and complete states remain distinct. |
| Settings | Units, equipment, personal guidance, appearance, account and privacy. | Server ownership; bounded authentication return; destructive account changes remain explicit and recoverable where possible. |

### Replace the visual system

Use warm porcelain `#F6F3E9`, forest `#183F35`, pale sage `#DCE6DB`, and a restrained ochre accent. Use one expressive display face for welcome/completion and a highly readable sans serif with tabular numerals for training. The HTML concept uses system fonts and Georgia so the report is standalone; final product font choices need licensing, loading, and legibility checks.

Use an 8-pixel spacing rhythm, 16–24-pixel content padding, compact set rows, and at least 48-pixel primary touch targets. Body text starts at 16 pixels; input values are larger. Labels remain visible above fields. Avoid thin decorative type for live data. Color supports explicit words and icons; it never carries state alone. Production contrast must meet WCAG AA, with visible focus and reflow checks.

On phones, the main action sits near the thumb without covering inputs or the software keyboard. On tablets, the active exercise remains primary with a compact routine sidebar. On desktop, use a constrained training column and optional detail pane rather than stretching forms. At 200% zoom, return to one readable column. Support reduced motion, keyboard operation, screen-reader announcements, and input error recovery from the start.

### Design new backgrounds, assets, and characters

<figure class="art"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="quiet set companion world" width="1536" height="1024" loading="lazy"><figcaption><strong>Original companion-world concept.</strong> Dawn studio background, Mica the kingfisher in attentive and resting poses, and equipment/milestone illustrations. These are art-direction assets; production needs individual exports and accessibility/performance QA.</figcaption></figure>

**Pip** is the primary stoat companion: ready beside a towel, quietly present before training, and resting after completion. **Mica** is a secondary kingfisher for recovery and reflective progress states. Neither gives technique instructions, reacts negatively to missed days, blocks controls, or implies a health assessment. Character selection is optional and can be turned off.

Create the following asset family as part of the redesign:

| Family | Deliverable specification | Placement and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment backgrounds | Dawn studio and quiet evening variant, wide and phone compositions with safe text zones. | Welcome and completion; solid opaque content surfaces preserve contrast. No busy imagery behind inputs. |
| Character artwork | Pip and Mica; ready, resting, complete, and neutral empty-state poses. Individual transparent exports plus source masters. | One bounded illustration per relevant screen. None in the active logging panel. No decorative overlap or focus target. |
| Equipment illustrations | Dumbbell, barbell, bench, mat, walking shoe, towel, timer, and distance marker. | Routine previews and setup; explicit text labels remain authoritative. |
| Functional icons | Consistent vector set for add, edit, back, play, pause, undo, check, history, and settings. | Actions use labels where ambiguity is possible; decoration has empty alternative text. |
| Background surfaces | Flat porcelain, sage panel, subtle low-contrast paper texture. | Texture at edges only; input and data surfaces stay quiet. |
| Milestone illustrations | Completion leaf and session summary art. | Reflect real completed work; no fake streaks, points, or shaming states. |
| Motion | Small confirmation transition and optional character idle. | No layout shift. Rest timing never depends on animation. Reduced-motion mode is static. |

The three supplied PNGs are concept boards/mockups. They establish original art and composition; they are not individual transparent sprites, final SVG icons, verified technique diagrams, or an optimized production asset pack. Use human-reviewed exercise references for instructional imagery. Do not ask generated characters to demonstrate safety-critical technique.

A production asset pass should export WebP/AVIF with PNG fallback where needed, use SVG for functional icons, reserve dimensions to prevent layout shift, and lazy-load nonessential art. Set a provisional 150 KB budget for a phone hero and 60 KB per character variant, then adjust from measured visual quality and network testing. Keep private guidance and owned account data out of public caches. These are targets, not measured sizes of the concept PNGs.

### Redesign the runner around the work

<div class="runner-board"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="quiet set runner concept" width="853" height="1844" loading="lazy"><div><span class="badge">Generated visual concept</span><h3>The set belongs in the first screen.</h3><p>Exercise name and target establish context. A compact set table makes progress legible. Large labeled fields support tired hands. One primary action saves the intended set and starts the configured rest. Demo access stays nearby without pushing inputs out of reach.</p><p>Keep a visible pending/saved state. The production design must preserve offline recovery and immutable history; a reassuring label is not a substitute for persistence.</p><p>The static image is an aesthetic reference. The interactive concept below explains the intended transitions with three simulated work sets. Neither is a tested production runner.</p></div></div>

<h2 id="prototype">Try the proposed flow</h2>

The simulation uses one short session with three bench-press sets. Start from Today, log a set, inspect rest, continue, and finish. The screen selector also previews setup, routine, guide, and progress. Data stays in this page’s memory and resets on reload. No account, network request, real workout, or video playback is involved. The rest display is illustrative; **Next set** advances it manually.

<div class="prototype-layout"><div><div class="eyebrow">Interactive recommendation</div><h3>One task at a time.</h3><div class="jump" id="screen-nav" aria-label="Concept screen selector"></div><button class="reset" id="reset-proto" type="button">Reset simulated session</button><p class="proto-status" id="proto-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">Simulated data only.</p></div><div class="proto-device" id="prototype-screen" aria-label="Workout app concept"></div></div>

<script>
(()=>{const screens=['Welcome','Setup','Today','Routine','Guide','Log set','Rest','Finish','Progress'];let state={screen:'Today',sets:[],weight:'10',reps:'10',error:'',finished:false};const el=document.getElementById('prototype-screen');const nav=document.getElementById('screen-nav');const status=document.getElementById('proto-status');const escape=s=>String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));const action=(label,target,quiet=false)=>`<button type="button" class="${quiet?'quiet':''}" data-go="${target}">${label}</button>`;const footer=()=>`<div class="proto-nav">${['Today','Routine','Progress'].map(s=>action(s,s,true)).join('')}</div>`;function render(){nav.innerHTML=screens.map(s=>`<button type="button" data-go="${s}" aria-pressed="${s===state.screen}">${s}</button>`).join('');let body='';const n=Math.min(state.sets.length+1,3);if(state.screen==='Welcome')body=`<div class="kicker">Quiet Set · concept</div><h3>Your next set.<br>A little clearer.</h3><p>A small place to plan, train, and see what you did.</p><div class="tile"><h4>Try a short session</h4><p>One movement. Three practice sets. No account needed in this simulation.</p></div>${action('Try one set','Log set')}${action('Create a routine','Setup',true)}`;if(state.screen==='Setup')body=`<div class="kicker">Make it yours</div><h3>Start with what you need.</h3><div class="tile"><h4>Short example</h4><p>Bench press · 3 sets · dumbbells and bench.</p></div><label for="proto-units">Display units</label><select id="proto-units"><option>Kilograms</option><option disabled>Pounds · production option</option></select><p>Equipment and targets are confirmed before saving. This preview does not create a routine.</p>${action('Use this example','Today')}${action('Preview routine editor','Routine',true)}`;if(state.screen==='Today')body=`<div class="kicker">Today</div><h3>${state.finished?'Good work today.':state.sets.length?'Pick up where you left off.':'Ready when you are.'}</h3><div class="tile"><div class="kicker">${state.sets.length&&!state.finished?'In progress':'Your routine'}</div><h4>Short session</h4><p>1 movement · 3 work sets<br>Dumbbells + bench</p>${action(state.finished?'View your session':state.sets.length?'Resume workout':'Start workout',state.finished?'Progress':'Log set')}</div><p>${state.finished?'Three saved sets are ready to review.':'Your routine and guidance stay available when you need them.'}</p>${footer()}`;if(state.screen==='Routine')body=`<div class="kicker">Routine</div><h3>Short session</h3><p>Saved · concept preview</p><div class="tile"><h4>Dumbbell bench press</h4><p>3 × 8–12 reps · 90 sec rest</p>${action('View movement and cues','Guide',true)}</div><p>A production editor would add, replace, reorder, and change targets here. This prototype demonstrates navigation only.</p>${action('Train this session','Log set')}${footer()}`;if(state.screen==='Guide')body=`<div class="kicker">Movement guide</div><h3>Dumbbell bench press</h3><p>Dumbbells + bench · standard variation</p><div class="tile"><h4>Cues in the real app</h4><p>Show the reviewed catalog instructions here. This design prototype does not generate exercise technique advice.</p></div><div class="tile"><h4>Watch demo</h4><p>On-demand player area. No video is loaded in this offline report; a real player needs a verified mapping and a working external fallback.</p></div>${action('Back to workout','Log set')}${action('Back to routine','Routine',true)}`;if(state.screen==='Log set'){const rows=Array.from({length:3},(_,i)=>`<div class="setrow"><span>Set ${i+1}${state.sets[i]?' · saved':i===state.sets.length?' · current':''}</span><span>${state.sets[i]?`${state.sets[i].weight} kg × ${state.sets[i].reps}`:'8–12 reps'}</span></div>`).join('');body=`<div class="topline"><span>Short session</span><span>Exercise 1 / 1</span></div><h3>Dumbbell bench press</h3><p>3 sets · 8–12 reps · 90 sec rest</p>${action('Movement guide','Guide',true)}${rows}<div class="bar"><i style="width:${state.sets.length/3*100}%"></i></div>${state.sets.length<3?`<form id="set-form"><div class="fields"><label for="proto-weight">Weight (kg)<input id="proto-weight" name="weight" type="number" min="0" max="500" step="0.5" inputmode="decimal" required value="${escape(state.weight)}"></label><label for="proto-reps">Reps<input id="proto-reps" name="reps" type="number" min="1" max="100" step="1" inputmode="numeric" required value="${escape(state.reps)}"></label></div><p role="alert">${escape(state.error)}</p><button type="submit">Log set ${n} &amp; rest</button></form>`:action('Review and finish','Finish')}<p>Simulated session · ${state.sets.length} of 3 sets logged</p>${state.sets.length?'<button type="button" class="quiet" data-undo>Undo last set</button>':''}${action('Exit to Today','Today',true)}`;}if(state.screen==='Rest')body=`<div class="kicker">Rest · illustrative timer</div><h3>A moment to reset.</h3><div class="timer">1:30</div><p style="text-align:center">No live countdown in this concept.</p><div class="success"><strong>${state.sets.length?'Set '+state.sets.length+' saved in the simulation':'No set logged yet'}</strong><p>${state.sets.length?state.sets.at(-1).weight+' kg × '+state.sets.at(-1).reps+' reps':'Return to the logger to try a set.'}</p></div>${action(state.sets.length>=3?'Review workout':state.sets.length?'Next set':'Log first set',state.sets.length>=3?'Finish':'Log set')}${action('Review logged sets','Log set',true)}`;if(state.screen==='Finish')body=`<div class="kicker">Session summary</div><h3>${state.sets.length===3?'You did the work.':'Your work so far.'}</h3><div class="success"><h4>${state.sets.length} sets · ${state.sets.reduce((a,s)=>a+s.reps,0)} reps</h4><p>${state.sets.length===3?'All planned work is logged.':'Complete the remaining sets before finishing this simulation.'}</p></div>${state.sets.length===3?'<button type="button" data-finish>Finish workout</button>':action('Return to workout','Log set')}${action('Review sets','Log set',true)}`;if(state.screen==='Progress')body=`<div class="kicker">Progress</div><h3>${state.finished?'A session to build on.':'Your work will appear here.'}</h3>${state.finished?`<div class="tile"><h4>Short session · completed</h4><p>${state.sets.length} sets · ${state.sets.reduce((a,s)=>a+s.reps,0)} reps<br>Dumbbell bench press</p></div><p>Real progress would compare actual comparable sessions. No invented streak or elapsed time appears here.</p>`:'<p>Finish the simulated session to see meaningful sets and reps, without irrelevant zero cards.</p>'}${footer()}`;el.innerHTML=body;status.textContent=`${state.screen} concept. ${state.sets.length} of 3 sets logged. ${state.finished?'Session completed.':'No real data is saved.'}`;}function go(s){state.screen=s;state.error='';render()}document.querySelector('.prototype-layout').addEventListener('click',e=>{const b=e.target.closest('button');if(!b)return;if(b.dataset.go)go(b.dataset.go);if(b.hasAttribute('data-undo')){const last=state.sets.pop();if(last){state.weight=String(last.weight);state.reps=String(last.reps)}state.finished=false;go('Log set')}if(b.hasAttribute('data-finish')){state.finished=true;go('Progress')}if(b.id==='reset-proto'){state={screen:'Today',sets:[],weight:'10',reps:'10',error:'',finished:false};render()}});el.addEventListener('input',e=>{if(e.target.name==='weight')state.weight=e.target.value;if(e.target.name==='reps')state.reps=e.target.value});el.addEventListener('submit',e=>{e.preventDefault();const form=e.target;if(form.id!=='set-form')return;const data=new FormData(form);const weight=Number(data.get('weight')),reps=Number(data.get('reps'));if(!Number.isFinite(weight)||weight<0||weight>500||!Number.isInteger(reps)||reps<1||reps>100){state.error='Enter a valid weight and a whole number of reps.';render();return}if(state.sets.length<3)state.sets.push({weight,reps});go('Rest')});render()})();
</script>

The bench-press concept illustrates weight and reps. The production runner must also support reps-only bodyweight work, timed holds, and distance/cardio targets with the relevant units and fields. Acceptance examples must cover 10 push-ups without load, a 30-second hold, and a 500-meter effort as well as a weighted set. Do not require irrelevant fields or treat missing load as missing work.

### Keep persistence and authorization honest

The redesign should reuse domain protections, not replace them with optimistic copy. Store weight in kilograms and distance in meters. Convert validated input and presentation at the boundary. Keep Firebase UID ownership on the server and never accept a client-supplied owner as authority. A saved routine creates a new revision; an active or historical workout retains its immutable snapshot.

Model UI states explicitly: draft, pending local save, server-confirmed save, retryable failure, rest running/paused, exercise complete, workout complete, and interrupted. Preserve input, set identity, queue order, and timer deadline across reload. A combined **Log set & rest** command must remain idempotent and must not advance twice on double-tap or retry. If the server rejects a save, retain the intended entry and show a recoverable error. Do not silently discard or relabel work.

The prototype intentionally demonstrates visual sequence only. Implementing these contracts requires domain tests and real browser recovery evidence; its in-memory behavior does not validate persistence or offline operation.

<h2 id="roadmap">An ordered recommendation plan</h2>

Delete unnecessary decisions first, simplify the remaining flow, optimize the repeated interaction, and automate only proven rules. Avoid a large visual reskin that leaves the same scroll and action costs intact.

| Order | Work | Outcome and acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · Correct misleading behavior | Fix Trainpal’s premature setup submission; remove unsupported progression copy; replace contradictory saved-state labels; distinguish skipped from unfinished. | Red tests reproduce each rule; step two makes zero POSTs; only explicit final submit creates once; History preserves actual intent. |
| 2 · Delete obstacles | Remove permanent home teaching blocks, internal IDs, revision essays, obligatory video pair UI, and fake blank movement. | In a moderated novice/returning-user study, at least four of five participants start or resume without coaching; empty draft is truly empty; public trial actually lets a visitor log a set. |
| 3 · Build the design system | Approve the complete screen hierarchy, typography, spacing, components, original backgrounds, Pip/Mica assets, icons, and motion. | Phone/desktop state matrix, contrast/focus/zoom checks, art safe zones, asset budgets, and all error/empty states reviewed. |
| 4 · Rebuild Today and runner | Resume/Start is first; combine save and rest; make next set/exercise explicit; move demos to a sheet. | At 390 × 844, Start/Resume and initial set fields/action are available without scrolling. Test keyboard, slow saves, double-tap, reload, timer suspension, offline queue, and retry. |
| 5 · Simplify routine and progress | Plain saved-state language, contextual chooser, actual sets/reps, meaningful trends. | Add/replace/cancel preserves context; one bodyweight session shows useful completed work; no invented elapsed time or tonnage. |
| 6 · Reconcile video truth | Compare source inventory with live data; separate provenance fields; resolve flagged variants; derive availability from actual records. | No duplicate seed; truthful review labels; selected-origin playback; single-demo fallback; source/docs/data alignment. |
| 7 · Automate proven maintenance | Metadata, duplicate, availability, and regression checks; targeted review queue. | Automation reports evidence and exceptions without manufacturing human approval. Recheck after provider/content changes. |

Before implementing, validate the navigation and runner with a small novice/returning-user study. Proposed targets: most participants start a session without coaching; a saved set and rest require one primary activation after entry; participants can find Resume after interruption; a person completing bodyweight work can explain what Progress records. These are acceptance goals, not observed study results or promised conversion gains.

### Recommended implementation boundaries

Keep reporting and policy proposals separate from execution. This report changes documentation only. A subsequent implementation plan should cover screen contracts, migration of any new draft/provenance types, authorization, feature rollout, and rollback. Introduce one flow at a time and retain immutable data compatibility. A full redesign does not require rebuilding the database or identity system from scratch.

The immediate evidence favors **a redesigned MWP using selective Trainpal improvements**, rather than treating either UI as the finished direction. That choice preserves MWP’s recent cleanup/history correction and avoids importing Trainpal’s onboarding regression. It remains a recommendation; no application code was ported or redesigned in this iteration.

| Trainpal source | `e09877895e135c06d5546a8538f2c80f48633265` |

The first development-server attempts caused recompilation/navigation-state ambiguity. Member findings use the stable production-built fixtures that replaced those attempts. The browser observation log retains chronology, including early attempts and immediate snapshots before navigation settled; those entries are not counted as successful journey evidence. Selected screenshots and the narrative identify the final states used for conclusions.

The following steps were actually exercised in both stable local apps: example setup, home, day start, save set, manual rest, select next set, enter a draft, reload, resume, save remaining sets, complete a movement, navigate onward, exit/resume, abandon, and view History. Separate fresh scopes exercised blank creation, canonical movement replacement, one-set publication, a completed workout, History, and Progress. Trainpal’s step-two submission was reproduced in both starting modes. Public example, library search, guide return, sample snapshot, and signed-out account boundary were inspected live.

**Exhaustive QA verdict: Incomplete.** This is a focused comparative product audit. It did not run a complete accessibility, keyboard, 200%-zoom, performance, physical-device, cross-browser, offline, multi-tab, network-failure, account lifecycle, ownership, or production-write battery. Console snapshots were collected but are not a clean-console release certification. The historical implementation QA remains a separate record. No timing, conversion, safety, or universal playback claim is inferred from this work.

**Independent self-critique:** eight journey themes drafted, eight kept, zero generic, zero duplicate. The review prompted target-specific runner inputs, more precise setup wording, and measurable user-study acceptance criteria.

The desired product should feel comfortable to hold and use between sets: a clear action, readable numbers, and a quiet companion outside the work area. Both audited apps have useful substance, but their density makes the person do too much interface management. The redesign earns its place only if it removes that effort.

- [Pip and art direction PNG](assets/companion-comparison/quiet-set-art-direction.png), [runner concept PNG](assets/companion-comparison/quiet-set-runner-concept.png), and [Mica/world PNG](assets/companion-comparison/quiet-set-companion-world.png): original generated concepts, not application screenshots.

Artwork was created with the built-in Image Gen tool for this report. The art-direction brief specified a calm porcelain/sage/forest/ochre gouache and screenprint style, an original stoat in ready/complete poses, a dawn studio, and quiet surfaces. The runner brief requested a phone workout view with exercise context, target/set table, large weight/reps fields, compact demo access, and one Log set & rest action. The companion-world brief requested a dawn studio with clear content space, original kingfisher in attentive/resting poses, and six coordinated equipment/milestone illustrations. No third-party character or private reference recording was used as an image input. Generation does not establish trademark clearance, technique accuracy, final accessibility, or production asset readiness.
